items.title: THE COMPLEXITY GAP: AI IN STRATEGIC HCM
items.abstract: The transition from traditional Personnel Administration to Strategic Human Capital Management (HCM) redefines human assets from operational costs to the primary source of sustainable competitive advantage. However, executing this strategic vision in a post-pandemic environment presents unprecedented challenges. This theoretical paper systematically reflects upon the literature mapping the evolution of HCM. It applies the Resource-Based View (RBV) and the VRIO framework to analyze the synergistic impact of modern trends: Employee Experience (EX), organizational agility, continuous learning, and inclusion. The conceptual synthesis reveals that implementing these modern HCM imperatives creates a systemic "complexity gap." Organizations face a limitation of scalability, where the cognitive and analytical capacities of traditional management are overwhelmed by the need for hyper-personalization and massive data volumes. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is identified as a theoretical necessity rather than a mere technological upgrade. AI systems provide the augmented intelligence required to bridge the complexity gap. However, the paper critically highlights that this integration must navigate significant ethical risks, including algorithmic bias and privacy concerns, to ensure sustainable human-AI symbiosis.

items.title: The Concentration of Artificial Intelligence in Big Tech and Its Implications for Human Rights in the European Union
items.abstract: The development of advanced artificial intelligence is increasingly concentrated in a small group of vertically integrated technology companies. These firms control combinations of computing infrastructure, cloud services, data, foundation models, software ecosystems, and channels of distribution. This article argues that such concentration transforms market power into a form of private governance over the conditions in which fundamental rights are exercised. Drawing on an interdisciplinary narrative review, it examines how concentration affects equality of access, privacy, freedom of science, working conditions, access to essential resources, environmental protection, and the availability of effective remedies. Evidence from data-centre expansion in Ireland, the United Kingdom, the United States, and Chile, together with studies of automation and collective bargaining, shows that benefits may be widely distributed while decision-making power and economic returns remain concentrated. Concentration does not itself establish a rights violation, but it increases dependency, opacity, switching costs, and the risk that social and environmental costs are externalised. The article concludes that competition policy must be combined with rights-based impact assessment, interoperability, public research capacity, worker participation, and enforceable access to review and remedy.

items.title: The duality of playful work design: A diary study of designing fun and competition
items.abstract: Although employees often have limited control over task assignments, schedules, or collaboration partners, they may still have discretion in how they carry out tasks. Building on Job Demands-Resources theory, we integrate information-processing perspectives of play to propose that playful work design – proactively adding elements of fun and competition to routine activities – can be useful even in tightly structured jobs by increasing activated positive affect and reducing exhaustion. We tested this proposition in a 20-day diary study among 57 Norwegian naval cadets, yielding 1,046 day-level observations, using multilevel structural equation modeling. On days when cadets designed their work playfully, they reported more activated positive affect and less exhaustion. Combining designing fun with designing competition amplified these benefits. Thus, small discretionary choices in how employees approach work may produce immediate well-being gains in low-discretion roles and offer a micro-level pathway through which play at work can support performance.

items.title: The Evolution of Attention in Large Language Models: Mechanisms, Trade-offs, and Emerging Trends
items.abstract: Self-attention gives LLMs fine-grained, query-dependent access to context, but dense token interactions incur quadratic prefill cost and a key--value cache growing with context length. Research thus spans explicit-memory compression, sparse access, recurrent state construction, structured state dynamics, and heterogeneous mechanism composition. This survey analyzes these developments as model-internal contextual memory. We introduce a five-dimensional lens---Memory Representation, Memory Update, Access, Readout, and Integration---describing what is represented, how it changes, what is query-eligible, how it is read, and how readouts form outputs. This lens compares overlapping research lines without imposing one computational model. We reconstruct mechanism-level developments and architectural adoption using 59 release-level records from 14 major model lineages and 11 high-performing open-weight endpoints. First, explicit-memory and recurrent-state methods retain distinct interfaces but increasingly control overlapping memory functions. Second, heterogeneous architectures increasingly coordinate across network depth: layer-wise composition distributes complementary memory processing across representational stages, while cross-layer reuse carries selected memory and routing artifacts forward. Depth thus becomes a dimension along which contextual memory is constructed and managed. Third, these developments motivate a stateful multidimensional memory-routing hypothesis: persistent memory is organized across temporal scope, network depth, substrate type, and representation granularity, while coordinated Sparse Write and Sparse Read determine what is maintained and what contributes to each query. Overall, efficient sequence architecture design increasingly concerns the organization, lifecycle, and selective use of contextual memory rather than an isolated Attention operator.

items.title: The fools are certain; the wise are doubtful: Exploring LLM confidence in code completion
items.abstract: Abstract Code completion entails the task of providing missing tokens given a surrounding context. It can boost developer productivity and serve as a code discovery tool. Code completion has recently been approached with Large Language Models (LLMs) fine-tuned on code (code LLMs). The performance of code LLMs can be assessed with downstream and intrinsic metrics. Downstream metrics are usually employed to evaluate the practical utility of a model, but can be unreliable and require complex calculations and domain-specific knowledge. In contrast, intrinsic metrics such as perplexity, entropy, and mutual information, which measure model confidence or uncertainty, are simple, versatile, and universal across LLMs and tasks, and have been proposed as proxies for functional correctness and hallucination risk in LLM-generated code. Motivated by this, we evaluate the confidence of LLMs when generating code by measuring code perplexity across programming languages, models, and datasets using various LLMs, and a sample of 2254 files from 881 GitHub projects. We find that strongly-typed languages exhibit lower perplexity than dynamically typed languages. Scripting languages also demonstrate higher perplexity. Shell appears universally high in perplexity, whereas Java appears low. Code perplexity depends on the employed LLM; under a fixed model, relative language-level rankings are largely stable across evaluation corpora. Although code comments modestly increase perplexity, the language ranking based on perplexity is barely affected by their presence. LLM researchers, developers, and users can use our findings to assess the suitability of LLM-based code completion in specific software projects based on how language, model choice, and code characteristics impact model confidence.

items.title: The Giving Of Reasons: Judgement Writing, Judicial Reasoning, and GenAI
items.abstract: This article focuses on the core judicial role of giving reasons for a judge’s decision and the use of generative artificial intelligence (‘GenAI’) tools based on LLMs in the crafting of judgments. Considering specifically GenAI and judgment writing in common law systems, it deals with the connection between the act of decision-making and the giving of reasons for that decision. Our argument is that judgment writing should remain the domain of human judges, for reasons that are both institutional (the impact on the judicial system) and individual or processual (the impact on judges performing their roles). We seek to analyse the nature and extent of judicial use of GenAI tools that preserves this as a human domain. Ultimately, we conclude that it is not appropriate to use GenAI for judgment writing, but peripheral or adjacent uses may be supportable, provided they do not undercut the core judicial role.

items.title: The Hybrid Residual–BiLSTM Model for Mitigating the Vanishing Gradient Problem in Synthetic Image Detection
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence has enabled the creation of highly realistic synthetic images, raising concerns regarding the authenticity of digital media. While convolutional neural network (CNN)-based methods have shown promising results for synthetic image detection, deep architectures often suffer from training instability caused by the vanishing gradient problem and limited representation learning. This study proposes a Deep Residual BiLSTM Fusion model that integrates residual-based CNN feature extraction with bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) modeling to enhance training stability and contextual representation learning. The proposed model is evaluated on the CIFAKE dataset, a challenging low-resolution benchmark for synthetic image detection. Experimental results demonstrate competitive performance with an accuracy of 97.27% and balanced precision and recall across both real and synthetic classes. Gradient flow analysis further confirms stable optimization behavior, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed hybrid architecture for robust synthetic image detection.

items.title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Different Aspects of the Society
items.abstract: Abstract In recent times, artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a revolutionary transformative force in various sectors of the contemporary society. It has rapidly becomes an integral part of our daily lives. Now a days AI plays crucial role in transforming various aspects of society and generate new possibilities and opportunities. The paper also present a dissection of an impact of AI on different aspects of the society including agriculture, industry, education, market, finance, business, transportation, employment, healthcare etc. This article is presented in a narrative review. The main object of this research paper is an attempt to find and to analyze the positive and negative impact of artificial intelligence on various field of the society. This research paper provides a comprehensive overview of the impact of AI on various aspects of the society in the form of dynamic nature of economy, transformation in education system, modern and advanced healthcare system, change in nature of employment and ethics etc. The collected literature for this research paper is focused on socio-economic influence as well as future fear and challenges in implementing of AI. The AI related literature shows that it has large potential to provide significant benefits for the present modern society but it has also aware us about challenges and risk in implementing of AI technology. Because of many scientists, technologists and others concerned with the welfare of society have started fearing about the extensive use of AI and its impacts on the society. The medical field is more affected by use of AI technology. It plays a crucial role in diagnosis, surgery, appropriate treatment methods and other related healthcare services. It can also play an important role in education transforming with student personalized learning experience for student and teacher also. However, we cannot ignore some problems about using of AI in the field of viability of employment, economic inequality, and ethical issues. In short, this research paper provides a comprehensive overview of the impact of AI on various aspects of the present society life.

items.title: The Impact of Duolingo-assisted Learning on Chinese Vocabulary Learning Motivation and Achievement among Elementary School Students
items.abstract: With the rapid development of mobile technology, mobile-assisted language learning has become increasingly prevalent in foreign language education. Duolingo is one of the most popular language learning applications. However, there is still limited evidence about its effectiveness in improving Chinese vocabulary learning, especially among primary school students. The purpose of this study is to examine the effects of Duolingo-assisted learning on Chinese vocabulary acquisition among primary school students and to examine students’ motivation toward Chinese vocabulary learning. A quantitative quasi-experimental design was adopted. Fifty primary school students participated in the study. A Chinese vocabulary pre-test and post-test were administered to measure learning achievement, while a learning motivation questionnaire was used to examine students’ motivation toward Chinese vocabulary learning. The results of a one-way ANCOVA revealed that students in the experimental group achieved significantly higher post-test vocabulary scores than those in the control group after controlling for pre-test scores. Furthermore, the results of a one-way MANOVA indicated that the experimental group demonstrated significantly higher self-efficacy motivation, whereas no statistically significant differences were found in intrinsic motivation, self-determination, or grade motivation. These findings suggest that Duolingo-assisted learning can effectively enhance Chinese vocabulary achievement and strengthen students’ confidence in learning Chinese vocabulary. The study provides empirical evidence supporting the integration of mobile-assisted language learning applications into primary Chinese language instruction and offers practical implications for teachers and educators.

items.title: The Impact of Organizational Ergonomics on Job Burnout: Evidence from Higher Education Institutions in Iraq
items.abstract: This research aims to examine organizational ergonomics and its impact on job burnout among a random sample of teaching and administrative staff employed at universities, colleges, and institutes within higher education institutions in Iraq. This topic is of considerable importance because improving organizational ergonomics can enhance the work environment, increase job performance, and promote employee well-being. The research also seeks to address the problem of occupational stress and excessive workloads resulting from increasing teaching and administrative tasks assigned to employees in higher education institutions. These pressures contribute to higher levels of job burnout and adversely affect employee performance and job satisfaction. A descriptive-analytical approach was adopted, and data were collected using a structured questionnaire administered to a random sample of teaching and administrative staff. A total of 108 valid questionnaires. The data were analyzed using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) and the Analysis of Moment Structures (AMOS) program. The results showed a statistically significant positive correlation and influence between the two variables. This finding contradicts the prevailing theoretical trend in the literature. This result suggests the possibility of other organizational or psychological factors influencing this relationship within Iraqi higher education institutions. Accordingly, the study recommends that decision-makers in Iraqi higher education institutions should move beyond the mere implementation of ergonomic practices and adopt a comprehensive approach that integrates improvements to the physical work environment with psychological and social support, while proactively managing employee expectations to reduce job burnout and enhance organizational effectiveness.

items.title: The Invisible Language Tax: Token Premiums of French and Regional Languages in 2026 LLM Tokenizers, and a French-Optimized Prototype
items.abstract: LLM services are billed per token and context windows are measured in tokens, yet the number of tokens needed for the same content varies across languages. We measure this token premium on seven tokenizers of widely used 2026 models (OpenAI o200k, Llama 3, Qwen3, DeepSeek V3/V4, Gemma 3, Mistral Tekken, and the Claude generation-5 tokenizer via Anthropic's counting API) on NTREX-128 (124 non-English reference translations) and on the Universal Declaration of Human Rights for regional languages. French requires 31% to 58% more tokens than English, whereas Simplified Chinese ranges from 5% fewer to 40% more and is cheaper than French on six of the seven tokenizers. Regional and overseas languages of France pay roughly 1.6 to 3.3 times the English count. We discuss how history re-sending, tiered pricing and fixed context windows amplify the absolute gap in agentic use. In a controlled experiment (BPE, Europarl, 50k vocabulary), adding French to tokenizer training data quickly reduces the premium, with diminishing returns and a growing cost for English. Finally, we present Baracoda FR v1.2, a byte-level BPE prototype with Tekken's vocabulary size. On a final test of six corpora never consulted during design, with a protocol declared fixed beforehand, it uses 11.5% fewer tokens than Tekken on French and 3.7% fewer on English; results hold after removing test sentences overlapping the training data and with an equal ordinary-token budget. It is worse on other languages and, at comparable vocabulary size, does not outperform CroissantLLM. These are segmentation results only; effects on model quality and task cost remain to be shown.

items.title: The Knowledge-Commerce Bridge (KCB) Framework: AI-Augmented Library Services for Inclusive Digital Entrepreneurship and Sustainable Innovation towards Viksit Bharat @2047
items.abstract: Abstract India’s Viksit Bharat @2047 vision requires a knowledge-driven digital economy powered by artificial intelligence, inclusive entrepreneurship, FinTech, e-commerce and sustainable practices. Library and Information Science (LIS) institutions remain under-utilised as active intermediaries between knowledge resources and the competencies demanded by the future of work. This paper coins the Knowledge-Commerce Bridge (KCB) Framework—an original, multi-layered LIS model that positions academic and public libraries as AI-enabled hubs for digital-commerce literacy, ethical information services and sustainable innovation. The study adopts a conceptual-constructive design that synthesises LIS theory, digital-economy literature, AI-ethics guidelines and national policy documents (NEP-2020, Digital India, Startup India). The KCB Framework comprises four interdependent layers: (1) Infrastructure and Multilingual Access, (2) AI Knowledge Processing, (3) User-Centric Commerce Services and (4) Ethical-Sustainable Governance. Expected outcomes include reduced information asymmetry for gig workers and micro-entrepreneurs, strengthened academia–industry–startup linkages, and measurable contributions to inclusive growth and the Sustainable Development Goals. The framework is offered as a replicable, emulable blueprint that other institutions can adapt, pilot and scale, thereby leaving a durable mark on both scholarship and practice.

items.title: The Legal and Ethical Challenges of Using Artificial Intelligence in Algeria
items.abstract: This study explores the legal and ethical problems arising from the integration of artificial intelligence technologies into the administrative and public-service systems of Algeria. It asks how far the country's existing legislative arsenal and its rules of digital ethics can absorb the accelerating development of intelligent systems, and assesses the role of the existing digital infrastructure in securing that transition. The paper adopts a descriptive-analytical methodology: the descriptive component inventories the relevant legal instruments and the available technical capacity, while the analytical component performs a gap analysis of whether texts drafted for classical digitisation can accommodate concepts such as the legal personality of a robot or liability for an algorithmic act, and subjects current digital administrative practice to critique against international ethical standards of transparency, fairness and non-discrimination. The study concludes that there is a clear legislative gap in the attribution of legal responsibility for algorithmic acts, particularly under the personal data protection legislation, because Algerian civil and criminal liability alike presuppose a discerning, willing human author whom an autonomous and opaque system does not supply. It further finds that the digital infrastructure, and specifically data centres and the national cloud, is the cornerstone of digital sovereignty and of ethical privacy, provided it is reinforced by an advanced cybersecurity framework and by reduced dependence on closed foreign platforms. The study recommends the drafting of a dedicated national legal framework and ethical charter for artificial intelligence, balancing technological innovation against the protection of the fundamental rights of the Algerian citizen.

items.title: The Moderating Effect of Digital Literacy on the Relationship between AI Interaction Quality and Consumer Emotional Engagement
items.abstract: As artificial Intelligence (AI) is having an increasing influence on the consumer-brand relationship, empirical evidence of the effects of AI-powered real-time communication on emotional brand engagement over time is scarce. Based on the Digital Emotional Brand Engagement (DEBE) model consisting of four outcome dimensions (Affective Engagement, Cognitive Engagement, Behavioral Engagement, Identification, and Emotional Attachment). The study proposes and empirically tests a model of four dimensions of AI interactions (Responsiveness and Availability, Personalization, Conversational Quality, Problem Resolution Efficiency). A descriptive-correlational quantitative design was adopted, and a sample of 400 consumers who had recently used AI-powered customer service was drawn. Multiple regression analysis and structural equation modeling (SEM) were used for analysis of the data, as well as mediation and moderation analysis (PROCESS macro). By considering all four dimensions of the interaction between people and artificial intelligence together, we could explain 52.1% of the variance in DEBE. The beta value for Affective Engagement was the largest for Responsiveness and Availability, while the highest beta value for Identification and Emotional Attachment was for Personalization. The overall path coefficient of the complete model from AI interaction to DEBE was 0.714. Partial mediation was observed between the quality of AI interaction and behavioral engagement with Identification and Emotional Attachment, and Digital Literacy had a significant moderating effect on the relationship between the quality of AI interaction and the emotional engagement of the consumer. The results highlight how critical an AI-powered customer service can be for boosting customers' emotional connection with brands in an e-marketing environment.

items.title: The Most Important Human Skills for the Age of AI and the Future of Work: FILE — The Five Intelligences of Leadership Evolution
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence changes what organizations can do; human leadership must decide what should be done, what remains accountable, and what must never be surrendered to machines. This working paper presents FILE: The Five Intelligences of Leadership Evolution as a human-centered management theory and diagnostic framework for responsible leadership and decision-making in the age of artificial intelligence and robotics. FILE argues that the most important human skills for the AI era and the future of work require the integrated exercise of five meta-intelligences: Augmented Intelligence, Emotional Intelligence, Cultural Intelligence, Political Intelligence, and Adaptive Intelligence. The paper defines the FILE formula, maps the framework onto the human hand, presents the 70 foundational nested intelligences, the 128-intelligence Teaching and Diagnostic Framework, and the 163-intelligence Extended Taxonomy, explains five emergent outcomes, and develops RC: The Relational Commons as the shared human ecosystem that leadership must protect, cultivate, and renew. It also clarifies boundaries among adjacent intelligences, offers a diagnostic application to AI-supported employee performance evaluation, and states limitations and future research directions. Its purpose is to establish a public, citable, and timestamped record of FILE as a transdisciplinary theory of human leadership in the age of AI and robots.

items.title: The permissibility and limits of the use of artificial intelligence in the system of state management of land resources of the Republic of Kazakhstan
items.abstract: The article is devoted to the study of the admissibility and limits of the use of artificial intelligence in the system of state management of land resources of the Republic of Kazakhstan. The main directions of implementing artificial intelligence technologies in cadastral and land management processes are examined, including the automation of geospatial data processing, forecasting changes in land use, and the integration of analytical results into managerial decision-making processes. Special attention is paid to the legal regulation of the use of artificial intelligence in land resource management based on the Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan dated November 17, 2025, No. 230-VIII “On Artificial Intelligence”. The application of specialized scripts containing elements of artificial intelligence for the automation of cadastral and land management activities is analyzed. Examples of the use of modern geographic information systems based on machine learning algorithms in spatial analysis and land monitoring tasks are presented. The article demonstrates the practical possibilities of applying artificial intelligence for calculating vegetation indices, automated monitoring of land resource conditions, and detecting violations in land use. The key advantages of AI implementation are identified, including improved data accuracy, reduced influence of the human factor, and optimization of time and material resources. The main problems and limitations associated with the digitalization of land relations are determined, including the need for data standardization, adaptation of the regulatory framework, and the development of methodological foundations for the application of artificial intelligence in the public law sphere.

items.title: The Relationship Between Artificial Intelligence Anxiety and Career Decidedness of Athletes
items.abstract: The aim of this study is to examine the relationship between artificial intelligence anxiety and career decidedness among athletes and to determine whether these variables differ according to certain demographic characteristics. The research was conducted with a sample of 392 athletes competing in different sports disciplines. The sample consisted of 122 female and 270 male athletes, with a mean age of 20.67 years. Data were collected using validated and reliable measurement tools, including the Artificial Intelligence Anxiety Scale (AIAS) and the Career Decidedness Scale (CDS). After confirming that the assumptions required for parametric analyses were met, descriptive statistics, independent samples t-tests, MANOVA, ANOVA, and correlation analyses were employed. The MANOVA results indicated a statistically significant difference only in the “artificial intelligence configuration” sub-dimension of the AIAS based on gender, with female athletes scoring higher than male athletes. Correlation analyses showed a low-level, negative, and statistically significant relationship between the “learning” sub-dimension of the AIAS and CDS scores (p < 0.05). Conversely, a low-level, positive, and statistically significant relationship was found between the “sociotechnical blindness” sub-dimension of the AIAS and CDS scores (p < 0.05). These findings suggest that athletes who experience higher levels of anxiety related to learning processes involving artificial intelligence tend to exhibit greater career indecision, whereas athletes who are less sensitive to the potential risks and threats associated with artificial intelligence technologies demonstrate greater decisiveness in their career choices. Future research may further expand on these findings by investigating the impact of awareness and education programs on athletes’ career decision-making processes.

items.title: The revenue halo effect: How revenues and expenses asymmetrically affect perceptions of profitability
items.abstract: There are two primary ways to boost profits: increase revenues or decrease expenses. For example, whether a company increases revenues by $1 million or decreases expenses by $1 million, its profits will increase by $1 million (all else equal). But how do people subjectively evaluate such changes to revenues and expenses, and what inferences do they draw as a result? Across nine experiments ( N = 6045), an archival data analysis, and four supplemental studies, we document a robust “revenue halo” effect: increases in revenues, relative to equivalent decreases in expenses, lead to more positive perceptions of profitability, in both the short and long run, and result in more favorable overall impressions of financial strength, performance, potential, and trajectory. Consequently, managers who propose ideas for increasing revenues (vs. decreasing expenses) are viewed as more competent; consultants who develop such strategies are more likely to be rehired; and companies that report higher revenues are more attractive to investors. We furthermore propose that the revenue halo effect can be explained, in part, by the belief that strategies for increasing revenues are more innovative than strategies for decreasing expenses. Finally, to underscore the real-world relevance of our account, we analyze approximately 13 million financial news articles, finding that when firms reported increased revenues (vs. decreased expenses), they subsequently rose in Fortune 's “World's Most Admired Companies” rankings (the following year). This research identifies a novel asymmetry in judgments of organizational performance, with implications for managerial decision-making, corporate communication, and capital allocation.

items.title: THE ROLE OF AI TECHNOLOGIES IN DEVELOPING THE PROFESSIONAL COMPETENCE OF ENGLISH LANGUAGE TEACHERS
items.abstract: This article analyses the role of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in developing the professional competence of English language teachers, their pedagogical potential, and the methodological conditions required for their effective use. In contemporary education, the development of AI technologies is transforming the content of teachers’ professional activities and bringing such areas as lesson design, educational material development, personalised learning, assessment, feedback provision, and pedagogical reflection to a new level. Systematic studies published in 2026 indicate that language teachers are using generative AI (GenAI) technologies for lesson planning, the development of educational materials, and the support of writing activities; at the same time, they reveal competency needs related to AI literacy, technical skills, ethical decision-making, and data privacy. The article also proposes a pedagogical model for developing English language teachers’ competence in working with AI technologies. Keywords: artificial intelligence, AI technologies, English language teacher, professional competence, AI literacy, digital competence, pedagogical competence

items.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Qur'anic Education and Interpretation: A Phenomenological Study of Its Requirements among Scholars in Fars Province, Iran
items.abstract: Purpose - This study examines the requirements for employing artificial intelligence (AI) in Qur'anic education and interpretation, focusing on how Qur'anic scholars and instructors in Fars Province, Iran, perceive the conditions necessary for its effective, ethical, and pedagogically appropriate use. Design/methodology/approach - The study adopts a qualitative phenomenological design using Colaizzi's seven-step analytical procedure. Data were collected through in-depth, semi-structured interviews with ten faculty members in Qur'anic sciences and Hadith and experienced Qur'anic instructors in Fars Province. Participants were selected through purposive and theoretical sampling until theoretical saturation was achieved. The interview data were subjected to thematic analysis, with credibility, dependability, confirmability, and transferability addressed through validation procedures. Findings - The analysis generated three principal categories: preliminary and infrastructural requirements, foundational and principled requirements, and technical and operational requirements. These comprised eight subcategories and 45 sub-concepts. The findings indicate that AI can support personalized learning, Qur'anic recitation, comprehension, multimodal instruction, and the integration of Qur'anic knowledge. However, its effective use requires reliable infrastructure, organized and credible Qur'anic data, trained educators, ethical safeguards, source verification, content validation, professional supervision, and interdisciplinary cooperation. Research implications/limitations - The framework provides practical guidance for educational institutions, Qur'anic centers, policymakers, and technology developers. However, the study is limited by its ten participants from a single province and its reliance on self-reported perceptions rather than observed AI-supported instruction. Originality/value - The study provides an empirically grounded phenomenological framework that connects AI, Qur'anic pedagogy, and ethical requirements for sacred-text education, extending AI-in-education research into the specific epistemic context of Qur'anic learning and interpretation.

items.title: The role of biomarkers and artificial intelligence in the personalized management of patients with chronic urticaria: from endotyping to predicting response to antihistamines (review)
items.abstract: Objective — to systematize current data on the endotypes and biomarkers of chronic urticaria (CU) and to analyze the potential applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in patient phenotyping, particularly in predicting response to antihistamines (AH) and other treatment modalities. Materials and methods. A literature search was conducted in the PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science databases for the period 2018—2025 using the key terms: «chronic urticaria», «biomarkers», «endotype», «artificial intelligence», «machine learning», «omalizumab», «antihistamines», and «treatment response». Forty-five sources meeting the inclusion criteria were selected. Results and discussions. The endotype concept of chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) — type I (autoallergic) and type IIb (autoimmune) — is key to understanding the clinical heterogeneity of the disease and provides the theoretical basis for biomarker profiling. Leading biomarkers include total IgE, IgG anti-FcεRI, IgG anti-TPO, the functional ASST and BAT assays, C-reactive protein, D-dimer, and basophil and eosinophil counts. Among AI-based tools, the most clinically validated is the prognostic calculator developed by J. Sánchez et al. (2024—2025), which predicts response to antihistamines with an accuracy of 78.6 % (AUC 0.829) based on 6 clinical variables, without requiring any laboratory tests. Conclusions. The combination of biomarker profiling and AI technologies offers a genuine path toward personalized management of patients with CU. Priorities include standardizing biomarker threshold values, external validation of predictive models, and establishing a regulatory framework for implementing AI in clinical practice.

items.title: The Role of Conscious Leadership in Reducing Job Alienation: An Analytical Study of the Opinions of a Sample of Employees at the Presidency of Sulaimani Municipality
items.abstract: Background: Job alienation is an important organizational issue that may negatively affect employees’ attachment to their work. However, the actual level of job alienation and its relationship with conscious leadership remain unclear, creating a practical need for investigation. Objectives: This study aims to examine the relationship between conscious leadership and job alienation among employees at the Presidency of Sulaymaniyah Municipality, assess the statistical relationship between conscious leadership and job alienation, and determine which dimensions make significant predictive contributions to job alienation. Methods: The study adopted a descriptive-analytical approach. The study population comprised approximately 520 employees, and 250 questionnaires were distributed, 233 were returned, and 220 valid questionnaires were retained for analysis. Data were collected using a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using SPSS version 25 through descriptive statistics, Cronbach’s alpha, Pearson’s correlation, and simple and multiple linear regression. Results: The findings showed that conscious leadership was perceived at a relatively high level, with Cognitive Awareness representing the most prominent dimension. Job alienation was at a relatively low to moderate level, with Normlessness being the most prominent dimension and Social Isolation the least prominent. A statistically significant negative relationship was found between conscious leadership and job alienation, and conscious leadership made a statistically significant negative contribution to the prediction of job alienation. At the dimensional level, Self-Awareness and Cognitive Awareness made statistically significant negative unique contributions, whereas Awareness of Others and Situational Awareness did not demonstrate statistically significant unique contributions. Conclusion: The findings indicate a statistically significant negative association between conscious leadership and job alienation. In particular, Self-Awareness and Cognitive Awareness made significant predictive contributions within the model, while the overall explanatory capacity remained limited, suggesting that other factors may also contribute to employees’ experiences of job alienation.

items.title: The Row Normalization Puzzle in Muon
items.abstract: This paper examines how row-wise renormalization affects Muon, focusing on the gap between NorMuon's worst-case guarantees and its practical performance (Li et al.). Despite its growing adoption and promising performance in large language model (LLM) pretraining, NorMuon's worst-case guarantees remain poorly understood. One fundamental question is: Does row normalization yield provable convergence gains, potentially through its interaction with approximate polar computation and exponential moving-average momentum? Our results show that row normalization introduces a dimension-dependent factor in the worst-case iteration complexity under the operator-norm geometry, which persists even with exact polar computation and any fixed momentum parameters. Indeed, we establish an algorithm-dependent lower bound and a matching upper bound in deterministic settings, and extend our upper bound analysis to stochastic settings. Both upper-bound analyses allow approximate polar computation. Experiments show that NorMuon is slower than Muon on synthetic problems inspired by our worst-case construction, yet outperforms Muon in LLM pretraining. These findings sharpen the puzzle of why row normalization helps in practice and complement the recent findings of Dewulf et al.

items.title: The safety and health plan for construction works: preventive planning tool or mere formal compliance
items.abstract: The construction sector is characterized by high organizational complexity derived from its temporary, dynamic, and process-specific nature. This industry registers some of the highest occupational accident rates worldwide. Within the European regulatory framework, Directive 92/57/EEC establishes the Health and Safety Plan (H&SP) as the principal instrument for preventive management on-site. In Spain, the transposition of this Directive introduced a preliminary design-phase document (Health and Safety Study or Basic Study, H&SS/H&SBS), intended to identify risks and define preventive measures that subsequently inform the contractor’s H&SP. Despite the importance of H&SS/H&SBS documents within the safety management process, empirical evidence remains limited regarding both their technical quality and their predictive capacity to explain the quality of subsequent H&SPs. This study addresses this gap through a qualitative and quantitative approach aimed at evaluating the intrinsic quality of H&SS/H&SBS and H&SP documents and modelling the dependency relationship between them. A database comprising 560 documents (280 H&SS/H&SBS and 280 H&SP) from 280 construction projects was assessed using a Delphi-based expert evaluation tool combined with a ratio weighting method. The results reveal consistently low levels of document quality and a limited capacity of H&SS/H&SBS to predict the quality of the corresponding H&SP. These findings suggest a systemic “cascade” failure in preventive planning, whereby documents frequently operate as instruments of formal compliance rather than as effective safety management tools. Our models’ findings support the need for effective audits and advanced technical training for professionals drafting these documents to improve preventive planning.

items.title: The Transformasi Proses Belajar pada Era Generative Artificial Intelligence: Sintesis Konseptual tentang Cognitive Offloading, Keterlibatan Kognitif, dan Integritas Akademik
items.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used by university students not only to locate information, but also to explain concepts, organize ideas, and complete academic tasks. This article examines the psychological processes that may explain why such use can support learning in some situations while reducing students' intellectual involvement in others. A conceptual literature review was conducted by bringing together foundational work on Distributed Cognition, Extended Mind, Cognitive Load, Student Engagement, and the ICAP Framework with recent studies on GenAI in education. Sources were selected for their relevance to cognitive offloading, cognitive engagement, and academic integrity. The review suggests that the educational consequences of GenAI depend less on its mere use than on how cognitive work is divided between students and the system. Offloading routine demands may free resources for evaluation and reflection, whereas delegating core reasoning may weaken engagement and make academic products less representative of students' own understanding. On this basis, the Educational Cognitive Transformation Model (ECTM) is proposed to connect learning transformation, cognitive offloading, redistribution of cognitive activities, cognitive engagement, learning quality, and academic integrity. ECTM is offered as a conceptual proposition that still requires empirical testing.

items.title: The trials methodology research agenda—an international multi-stakeholder priority setting exercise
items.abstract: Abstract Background Trials methodology research priorities must be regularly reassessed to address contemporary methodological challenges. Over a decade has passed since the original priority setting exercise surveyed UK clinical trials unit directors. We conducted a two-stage international, multi-stakeholder survey to identify and rank current priorities in clinical trial methodology. Methods Stakeholders—researchers, trialists, healthcare professionals, patient and public representatives, funders, research ethics committee members, and others—were recruited through professional networks and snowball sampling. In stage 1, participants responded to four open-ended questions covering trial planning, conduct, analysis, and reporting. Responses were categorised into 34 research questions. In stage 2, participants reviewed the questions in random order, selected their top 10, and ranked them. Reverse scoring was applied, with scores summed within stakeholder groups, converted to rank-based scores, and combined so each group contributed equally regardless of size. Additional questions were independently coded by two authors against the 34 predefined questions, and new themes identified. Results In stage 1, 274 participants from 20 countries provided 2409 suggestions, categorised under 34 research questions. In stage 2, 431 respondents from 25 countries participated, of whom 341 (79%) across seven stakeholder groups completed priority ranking. The top 10 priority questions (including a joint seventh rank) were (1) designing relevant and impactful trials, (2) ensuring representative participants, (3) improving recruitment, (4) identifying and prioritising outcomes, (5) using healthcare systems data, (6) participant involvement in planning, (7=) transparency of trials, (7=) optimising trial approvals, (9) reporting and presenting findings, and (10) sharing and communicating findings. items.title: The Use of AI Software in Reviewing Applicants for General Surgery Residency
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools are increasingly used to improve efficiency, including in residency application review. While these technologies may streamline processes, their ability to identify optimal candidates for specific programs remains uncertain. This study aims to evaluate if AI can enhance the productivity of residency application review without compromising selection quality. METHODS: General surgery residency applications were analyzed using a large language model-based AI platform configured with customized program-specific weighting of applicant metrics. The AI-generated scores and rank list were compared with results from the traditional review process in which the application review committee manually reviews applications, scores applicants, and selects candidates for interview. RESULTS: A total of 847 applications were reviewed, and 96 applicants were manually selected (MS) for interviews by the application review committee. Of these, 32 (33%) were also ranked in the AI's top 96 candidates, including 7 in the top 10. Quartile analysis demonstrated that 51 (53.1%) MS candidates were in the top quartile of AI rankings, 26 (27.1%) in the second, 8 (8.3%) in the third, and 11 (11.4%) in the bottom. Adjusting the weights of various factors did not significantly alter these distributions. Technical review revealed scoring anomalies, including negligible AI scores for some candidates selected for interview. Analysis of the weighted factors showed that letters of recommendation contributed 29.4% of MS vs 25.1% of AI scoring (p = 0.009), research 6.3% vs 8.0% (p = 0.017), MSPE 7.4% vs 9.0% (p = 0.073), and factors such as USMLE and experiences were equivalent between the 2 groups. CONCLUSION: AI-assisted review may serve as a useful adjunct for initial screening but requires further refinement and training to better replicate human qualitative judgment. Future work will include evaluating concordance between AI rankings and the final program rank list and additional application review to guide software optimization and improve reliability as a screening tool.

items.title: The use of ergonomics methods in logistics process - case study
items.abstract: Ergonomics, as a scientific discipline, is gaining increasing importance in modern workplaces, as people spend more time engaged in work-related activities, often in static postures and under continuous technological exposure. Ergonomics focuses on adapting working conditions to match the physical and mental capabilities of humans, with the primary goals of enhancing productivity, ensuring safety, and improving overall employee well-being. Proper ergonomic practices help prevent workplace injuries, reduce fatigue, and create a healthier and more efficient work environment. One of the key roles of ergonomics is to reduce human fatigue during work processes. By designing tasks, tools, and workspaces that align with human capabilities, ergonomics minimizes unnecessary physical and mental strain. This not only improves worker comfort and health, but also contributes to clearer and more realistic standards for performing operations. As a result, ergonomics plays a vital role in increasing labor productivity and maintaining long-term efficiency in production environments. The emergence of new Industry 4.0 technologies such as automation, digitization, and artificial intelligence presents additional challenges for ergonomics. These rapid technological advancements require ongoing ergonomic adaptations to ensure safe, healthy, and sustainable work practices. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the field of ergonomics and presents key ergonomic methods. Special attention is given to the software solution ErgoFellow 3.0, which includes various tools to assess and implement ergonomic improvements. The use of computer-aided ergonomics enables quick, accurate evaluations of working conditions, supporting a safer and more productive workplace.

items.title: THE VICIOUS CYCLE OF DIGITAL ESCAPISM: A LITERATURE REVIEW ON ONLINE GAMING ADDICTION, OCCUPATIONAL BURNOUT AND PRODUCTIVITY AMONG YOUNG ADULT PROFESSIONALS
items.abstract: Introduction: Occupational burnout among young adult professionals has reached concerning levels, and there are more people struggling with internet gaming disorder (IGD) each day. Studies suggest these two problems feed into each other. Burnout can drive people toward gaming as an escape, and gaming can reduce work performance, which in turn increases burnout. This literature review was conducted to discuss how occupational burnout, gaming addiction, and work performance relate to one another among young professionals. Methods: We searched the MEDLINE, PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases from 2001 to 2025. Results: We included 52 relevant studies, and the findings show that each part of the cycle reinforces the others. Burnout increases escapism behaviors (r = 0.31-0.65), and escapism motivation is the strongest predictor of IGD among gaming motivations (r = 0.40); it also bridges the relationship between work stress and pathological gaming. Discuss: Most of the studies conclude that a vicious cycle exists where burnout could become gaming addiction through digital escapism, and gaming addiction decreases work productivity and then leads back into burnout. Digital escapism appears to be a crucial link in the chain. Addressing these problems requires intervention at multiple levels, organizational changes alongside individual support. Longitudinal research testing actual interventions would be a valuable next step. Conclusion: Growing interdependence between digital wellness and occupational health necessitates coordinated, multilevel interventions targeting individual, behavioral, organizational, and structural determinants. Given the substantial individual and economic burden, greater investment in longitudinal research, policy development, and rigorously evaluated interventions is essential.

items.title: Therapeutic Efficacy of Rajayoga Meditation and Varma Therapy in Attenuating Occupational Stress and Reversing Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease among Night-Shift Information Technology Professionals
items.abstract: The growing incidence of Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD) among night-shift IT professionals is posing as a major occupational health issue since shift work, sedentary lifestyle, psychosocial stress, lack of sleep, and disrupted circadian rhythms can lead to metabolism problems and fatty liver. Even though there is a possibility to cure NAFLD by adopting lifestyle changes, the pharmacological intervention for NAFLD is minimal and there is a high potential for the use of mind-body techniques like Rajayoga Meditation and Varma Therapy to enhance metabolic, psychological, and physiological well-being. The present study intended to determine the efficacy of Rajayoga Meditation and Varma Therapy on occupational stress and NAFLD among night-shift IT professionals. An interventional study was performed among 60 IT workers on night shift (aged between 25 and 45 years; 30 males and 30 females) suffering from NAFLD (Grades I and II), who participated in a protocol involving Rajayoga meditation and Varma therapy for a duration of 12 weeks. Parameters measured included Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10), serum cortisol, lipid profile, levels of anxiety and depression, which were measured using the Depression Anxiety Stress Scale-21 (DASS-21), and status of liver, as determined by ultrasound scanning. Data analysis involved paired statistical test, with p<0.001 being regarded as statistically significant. Significant improvement was seen post-intervention in all the parameters mentioned above, including Perceived Stress Scale score, serum cortisol level, lipid profile levels, DASS-21 scores for anxiety and depression, and ultrasonography-based NAFLD grading. The results showed that Rajayoga meditation and Varma therapy could lead to significant improvements in psychological well-being, stress-related biomarkers, lipid metabolism, and NAFLD-related ultrasonographic features among night-shift IT professionals.

items.title: Three Rounds on Emergent Analogy: What the Webb, Hodel-West and Lewis-Mitchell Exchange Settled, How Its Third Round Tested a System While Still Claiming the Model, and Whether 'Counting' Names the Step That Analogy Theory Calls Inference
items.abstract: (c) 2026 Pranay Mahendrakar. Licensed under CC BY 4.0. In 2023 a large language model was reported to solve text-based analogy problems zero-shot at or above the level of college students. Two critiques followed. They showed that performance on letter-string analogies collapses when the alphabet is permuted or replaced by symbols, while human performance does not. The original authors replied that the failures come from an auxiliary difficulty with counting, and that GPT-4 solves the permuted problems at a human level once it can write and execute code. This paper reads all three rounds in full, including the preprint and published versions of the reply, and sorts their claims into three groups. Settled: the replications agree, and the unaided model fails the counterfactual variants under answer-only prompts. Moved: the evidence. The third round's decisive result is for a model-plus-interpreter system, while its title claim remains about language models. Unsettled: which operations count as auxiliary, and whether the models represent the new alphabet at all. Published checks from both sides, run in different studies with different alphabets, suggest splitting "counting" into two operations: GPT-4 names the one-step successor of a letter in a permuted alphabet almost perfectly, but identifies the interval (of up to two steps) between two given letters about one time in ten. A study of four newer models, however, finds every model worse at naming items two steps away, and its authors conclude that the models do not build representations of novel alphabets on the fly. If the difficulty lies in recognising the relation in the source pair, it lies in what componential theories of analogy call inference; if it lies in representing the order, it lies in encoding, which the same theories also count as part of analogy. On that decomposition, either way, the reply's "auxiliary" label is not yet earned. The paper states a procedure for reading capacity claims from counterfactual tasks, in which the decomposition of the task is fixed before data are seen, and proposes five experiments on existing materials that could decide between the readings. Every number in it is taken, or summed, from the published sources.

items.title: Throw-Ins in Soccer: Current Insights, Tactical Relevance, and Practical Recommendations for Practitioners. A Systematic Review
items.abstract: This study was designed as a systematic review to identify, critically appraise and synthesise the available evidence concerning throw-ins in association football. The scope of the review was deliberately broad because the existing literature does not treat the throw-in as a single, homogeneous performance variable. Instead, the evidence addresses complementary dimensions ranging from the regulatory and biomechanical constraints of the action to its temporal management, offensive organisation, defensive responses and contribution to subsequent attacking outcomes. Accordingly, the review sought to integrate these dimensions within a single evidence framework while maintaining clear distinctions between technical, tactical, contextual and outcome-related findings. The review was reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 statement (PRISMA 2020; Page et al., 2021), and the identification and reporting of information sources and electronic search procedures were additionally guided by the PRISMA extension for searches (PRISMA-S; Rethlefsen et al., 2021).[KS6.1][DP6.2][Á6.3] The review was structured around an adapted Population–Exposure–Comparator–Outcome framework appropriate for observational and performance-analysis research. The population comprised male and female association-football players and teams across youth, amateur, semi-professional, professional and international competitive contexts; the exposure was a throw-in occurring during association football; comparators, when applicable, comprised alternative technical executions, tactical organisations, contextual conditions or competitive environments; and outcomes encompassed biomechanical, temporal, tactical, possession, territorial, defensive and attacking indicators directly related to throw-ins. The primary research question was: What is known about the technical, temporal, tactical and performance-related characteristics of throw-ins in association football, and which contextual factors appear to influence their effectiveness? Five secondary research questions were specified to reflect the principal thematic structure of the review: (1) What regulatory and biomechanical characteristics define the execution of a throw-in, and which technical factors influence throwing performance? (2) How are throw-ins related to playing time, restart duration and strategic management of match tempo? (3) Which offensive tactical strategies and contextual factors are associated with successful possession retention, progression and attacking outcomes following a throw-in? (4) How do defending teams organise and respond to throw-ins, and which contextual factors influence pressure, recovery and subsequent transitions? (5) What is the contribution of throw-ins to goal scoring and shot creation, both directly and through the subsequent possession? These questions were selected to ensure that the review did not reduce throw-in effectiveness to a single endpoint such as possession or goals. In particular, the review considered that direct goals are a relatively distal and infrequent outcome, whereas first contact, possession retention, territorial progression, shot creation and defensive recovery may represent more sensitive intermediate indicators of performance. The primary objective was therefore to synthesise the evidence across these interconnected levels and determine the practical relevance of the throw-in as a phase of play. The protocol was not prospectively registered. Nevertheless, the review procedures were systematically developed, documented and operationalised throughout the review process. Eligibility criteria, study-selection procedures, data-extraction domains, methodological-appraisal procedures and the synthesis framework were defined and progressively refined prior to their application to the final evidence set, with all decisions documented in the master evidence database to ensure transparency, consistency and reproducibility. 2.2. Eligibility criteria Eligibility criteria were predefined according to the research questions and were applied at both title-and-abstract and full-text screening stages. Population and context Studies were eligible when they examined male or female players or teams participating in 11-a-side association football. Youth, amateur, semi-professional, professional and international competitive levels were eligible. Studies conducted in futsal, beach soccer, rugby, Australian football, Gaelic football, American football, robotic football or other sports or football formats were excluded. Exposure The exposure of interest was a throw-in performed during association football or analysed in a context intended to evaluate its technical, biomechanical, temporal, tactical, defensive or match-performance characteristics. Throw-ins were required either to constitute the primary phenomenon under investigation or to form an independently analysable category within a broader study of match interruptions, set pieces, possession, playing time, passing, defensive behaviour, shot creation or goal-scoring patterns. Studies in which throw-ins were mentioned only incidentally and for which no independently extractable throw-in-specific information was available were excluded. Comparators A formal comparator was not required for descriptive or biomechanical studies. Relevant reviews were not considered eligible studies for the evidence synthesis but were retained as complementary sources for contextualisation and backward and forward citation searching. items.title: Towards a sociotechnical framework and maturity model for artificial intelligence-driven supply chain due diligence
items.abstract: Objective: The objective of this article is to develop an integrated sociotechnical framework and a diagnostic maturity model for artificial intelligence-driven supply chain due diligence. It addresses the implementation gap under escalating mandatory regulations by demonstrating how technological capabilities, ethical governance, and cultural adaptation interact, shape each other, and must be developed together. Research Design & Methods: We employed a theory-building approach and conducted a purposive literature synthesis. We applied thematic analysis, grounded in institutional theory, stakeholder theory, and the technology-organisation-environment framework to develop an integrated framework and maturity model, illustrated via analysis of European e-commerce sustainability disclosures. Findings: We identified three critical sociotechnical interfaces (tech-ethics, ethics-culture, and tech-culture) and derived three formal propositions from the analysis. We propose, organisational readiness may function more as a coefficient than an additive factor, where the substantive effectiveness of technological tools depends on cultural commitment. A distinct ‘institutional governance gap’ emerges from the illustrative application. Implications & Recommendations: Organisations, including small and medium-sized enterprises and entrepreneurial ventures operating within mandatory due diligence supply chains, should move beyond techno-centric approaches to assess artificial intelligence (AI) readiness simultaneously across operational, institutional, global, and strategic layers. The maturity model enables systematic capability gap identification. Contribution & Value Added: We propose a diagnostic maturity model and formal propositions that bridge the gap between legal theory and organisational implementation. These contributions are conceptual and require empirical validation.

items.title: Towards foundation-style models for energy-frontier heterogeneous neutrino detectors via self-supervised pretraining
items.abstract: Abstract Accelerator-based neutrino physics is entering an energy-frontier regime in which interactions reach the tera-electronvolt scale and produce exceptionally dense, overlapping detector signatures. Event interpretation is impractical for conventional reconstruction and challenging for supervised models trained from scratch, particularly when labelled data are scarce and analyses span diverse objectives. Here we present a sparse Vision Transformer framework for learning reusable representations from heterogeneous detector data. Self-supervised pretraining combines masked-autoencoder reconstruction with relational voxel-level objectives for hierarchy, ghost and particle identification, followed by joint fine-tuning across classification and regression tasks. On simulated events from the proposed FASER calorimeter (FASERCAL) concept, pretraining improves neutrino-flavour and charm-quark identification, momentum regression and vertex reconstruction, with relational objectives providing further gains in topologically complex channels. Attribution and representation diagnostics show a more structured latent space, while detector-subsystem ablations recover physically plausible channel-dependent roles. With roughly 10 3 labelled events, the pretrained encoder matches the flavour-classification performance of scratch training with an order of magnitude more data. Cross-domain transfer is observed on public plastic-scintillator and liquid-argon benchmarks. A matched alternative-generator stress test shows stable flavour and kinematic performance while exposing charm tagging as generator sensitive. These results support self-supervised multimodal pretraining as a route towards reusable detector representations. We use ‘foundation-style’ in this restricted sense, rather than claiming a completed general-purpose detector foundation model.

items.title: Towards Hierarchical Cyber Defense with Large Language Models: From Planning to Execution
items.abstract: An autonomous cyber defender trained with reinforcement learning (RL) is typically tied to the network on which it was trained, limiting its ability to generalize as network scale changes. Hierarchical RL reduces decision complexity by separating strategic targeting from tactical execution, but it does not eliminate this retraining dependence. We investigate whether frozen, zero-shot large language models (LLMs) can provide retraining-free control in hierarchical cyber defense and how performance changes as LLM control is extended from planning to execution. We formulate a controller-agnostic planner-executor hierarchy in which the planner selects a subnet to defend over a fixed horizon and the executor selects defensive actions within that subnet. Using the high fidelity Cyberwheel environment, with its built-in automated red team agent mapped to the MITRE ATT&CK framework, we compare RL+RL, LLM+RL, and LLM+LLM configurations using six models ranging from 3B to 70B parameters, including two cybersecurity-specialized models, across small, medium, and large networks. Replacing only the planner with an LLM yields limited gains as network size increases. In contrast, extending LLM control to execution produces notable improvements for sufficiently capable models. For instance, a frozen general purpose 70B model holds successful lateral movement to approximately 1% of steps and attacker impact near zero across all three network scales using the same model weights, while the RL baseline is retrained for each scale. Our results show that sufficiently capable frozen LLMs can maintain strong defensive performance across the evaluated network scales without task-specific retraining, while also indicating that strong tactical execution is important to realizing the benefits of LLM-based control.

items.title: Towards Proactive Medication Safety: Artificial Intelligence-Based Prediction, Detection, and Prevention of Drug-Related Problems in Clinical Practice
items.abstract: Abstract Background Medication-related problems, including adverse drug reactions (ADRs), adverse drug events (ADEs), drug–drug interactions (DDIs), medication errors, and inappropriate antimicrobial use, remain important challenges in clinical practice. Artificial intelligence (AI) has developed rapidly and may help healthcare professionals identify medication-related risks earlier. Previous studies have reported the use of machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, and newer generative AI methods in pharmacovigilance, drug-interaction prediction, clinical decision support, and antimicrobial stewardship. Objective This study aimed to review AI's role in predicting, detecting, and preventing drug-related problems and to compare its applications across pharmacovigilance, drug–drug interaction prediction, clinical decision support, medication safety, and antimicrobial stewardship. Methods We conducted a literature review of 39 selected articles on AI and medication safety. The literature was organised into major areas, including ADR/ADE prediction and pharmacovigilance, DDI prediction, clinical decision support, generative AI and EHR-based medication safety applications, and antimicrobial stewardship. The findings were compared according to AI methods, clinical purpose, safety application, benefits, and major limitations. Results The reviewed literature shows that AI can analyse large amounts of clinical and medication data to identify patients at risk of ADRs and ADEs, detect possible DDIs, support medication decisions, and improve pharmacovigilance. Machine learning and deep learning methods have shown promising results in prediction and classification tasks. AI has also been used to support antibiotic selection, antimicrobial resistance prediction, and antimicrobial stewardship. Generative AI and large language models are emerging in DDI identification, clinical decision support, and pharmacovigilance. However, most studies remain retrospective, and external validation and prospective clinical testing are still limited. Conclusion AI has strong potential to support a proactive medication-safety system by predicting risks, detecting problems early, and supporting preventive action. However, AI should support rather than replace healthcare professionals. Future research should focus on high-quality data, external validation, explainable AI, patient privacy, clinical integration, and real-world testing. The ultimate goal should be to develop safe, reliable, and patient-centred AI systems that help reduce medication-related harm and improve clinical outcomes. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence; Medication Safety; Drug-Related Problems; Pharmacovigilance; Adverse Drug Reactions; Drug–Drug Interactions; Clinical Decision Support Systems; Antimicrobial Stewardship

items.title: Tracing the Path from Self-Efficacy to Artificial Intelligence Use: The Mediating Role of Technology Acceptance Among Mathematics Undergraduates in Nigeria
items.abstract: The way students learn, engage with, and create information has changed as artificial intelligence (AI) becomes more common in classrooms. Therefore, understanding the factors that influence students' adoption of AI tools is vital to improving learning outcomes, especially in disciplines that require extensive mathematics. This study examined the mediating role of technology acceptance in the relationship between self-efficacy and AI use among mathematics undergraduates in Nigeria. We used a quantitative cross-sectional design and collected data from 256 students across three public universities in Southwestern Nigeria using a structured survey instrument. We operationalised technology acceptance solely as perceived ease of use, rather than as the full set of constructs typically represented in the Technology Acceptance Model. Data were analysed using PLS-SEM. The findings showed that self-efficacy significantly and positively relates to both technology acceptance (β = 0.591, t = 9.166, p < .05, f² = 0.537) and AI use (β = 0.301, t = 4.727, p < .05, f² = 0.092). Technology acceptance also significantly relates to AI use (β = 0.371, t = 5.093, p < .05, f² = 0.140) and partly mediated the relationship between self-efficacy and AI use. The model explained 35.0% of the variance in technology acceptance (R² = 0.350) and 36.1% of the variance in AI use (R² = 0.361), while both endogenous constructs demonstrated predictive relevance (Q² > 0). The findings suggest that mathematics educators can support AI use by strengthening students’ technological self-efficacy and ensuring that AI tools are easy to use within mathematics learning activities. Theoretically, the findings indicate that perceived ease of use provides an important mechanism through which self-efficacy relates to students’ AI use, while also highlighting the need to distinguish this specific acceptance dimension from broader technology acceptance models.

items.title: Training LLM Judges from Language Feedback via Position-Selective Self-Distillation
items.abstract: We study training LLM judges from natural language feedback, especially for subjective tasks where the verdict depends strongly on which evaluation criteria the judge invokes and how it weighs them. The dominant approach, outcome-supervised RL (e.g., GRPO), credits every token in the rollout with a single scalar determined only by the accuracy of the final verdict, providing no separate credit at the criterion-choice tokens and ignoring the rich language feedback (e.g., preference rationales) that naturally accompanies preference labels. Self-Distillation (SD) is one natural way to use this language feedback: the same model, conditioned on this feedback, acts as a teacher providing dense, position-level supervision. However, not all positions carry equally useful signal. Using the per-position entropy shift between teacher and student, we identify two regimes: context sharpening, where the teacher concentrates probability on a particular feedback-aligned criterion expression, and context spreading, where the teacher distributes probability across multiple feedback-aligned alternatives. We interpret these patterns as follows: sharpening encourages memorization of a particular criterion expression, whereas spreading promotes semantic understanding by preserving these alternatives. Motivated by this asymmetry, we introduce position masking based on the entropy shift that retains the lower tail of the entropy-shift distribution. items.abstract: Subject. The behavioral aspect of the transformation of the financial decision‑making process by an institutional venture investor in the form of a classic financial venture fund under conditions of digitalization (in the context of the spread of artificial intelligence (AI). Objectives. To examine the transformation of the decision‑making process by institutional venture investors using AI technologies. To identify and classify the causes of the spread of unreliable information in the financial market. To determine the nature of the influence of behavioral effects on venture investors' decision‑making under conditions of declining quality of the information base used for AI training. Methods. General scientific methods were applied, including generalization, argumentation, analysis, synthesis, and classification. Results. The causes of the spread of unreliable information on the Internet were identified and ranked by level of significance. The concept of a "disinformation spiral" was proposed. It is this spiral that underlies the possible intensification of the negative influence of certain behavioral factors and prevents the complete elimination of irrational actions by venture investors through the use of AI technologies. Conclusions and Relevance. The influence of the quality of the information base used for AI training on the level of impact of various behavioral effects on venture investors was substantiated. A decline in the quality of the information base can be regarded as an additional factor in the formation of vulnerabilities in the financial system. The results can be used by financial market participants to assess the risks of using AI technologies, as well as by developers and users of software products to improve the quality of the information base for AI training.

items.title: TRANSFORMING KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATOR (KPI) TRACKING IN HIGHER EDUCATION THROUGH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND MACHINE LEARNING: THE APPLICATION OF THE PREMIER SCORE INDEX (PSI) IN HIGHER EDUCATION
items.abstract: The rapid digital transformation in higher education has exposed a critical flaw in institutional governance: traditional Key Performance Indicator (KPI) tracking methods that reliant on manual data entry, siloed systems, and static reports are increasingly obsolete and lack the precision, adaptability, and responsiveness needed in today's data-intensive environments. To address this pressing need for data-driven evaluation tools, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) are fundamentally transforming performance management by introducing real-time analytics, strategic alignment, and Data-informed decision-making. This study explores the development and application of the Premier Score Index (PSI), a novel, weighted composite metric assessing institutional performance across five strategic domains: Teaching, Research, Community Service, Professional Service, and Academic Reputation. Through a systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis from 2010 to 2024, the paper identifies how AI/MLenhance KPI tracking across its lifecycle: development, monitoring, and reporting. Findings reveal the potential of AI-driven KPI systems, such as the PSI, to revolutionize institutional planning and accountability, positioning academic institutions to thrive in a rapidly evolving digitallandscape.
